text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

Both you and the successful candidate are women, meaning sex discrimination is extraordinarily unlikely to explain why she was selected over you. An all-female panel selecting one woman over another provides no viable basis for a sex bias claim, and bringing it up will only undermine your credibility. 

Instead, focus on procedural transparency and qualifications. You appear to have significantly stronger administrative credentials—a master's degree in educational leadership and five years as deputy principal—compared to the successful applicant's teaching background. Follow up politely on your pending request for a written explanation, and evaluate your next steps based strictly on merit, advertised criteria, and hiring policies rather than the panel’s gender.
